Hindu Succession Act, 1956
Section 6 Devolution of interest in coparcenary property On and from the commencement of the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, in a Joint Hindu family governed by the Mitakshara law, the daughter of a coparcener shall by birth become a coparcener in her own right in the same manner as the son. Any coparcenary property shall be divided equally among all legal heirs and coparceners through a decree or registered deed of partition.
Section 8 General rules of succession in the case of males The property of a male Hindu dying intestate shall devolve firstly upon the heirs being the Class I relatives specified in the Schedule, including sons, daughters, widow, and mother, all taking equal shares simultaneously.
Section 14 Property of a female Hindu to be her absolute property Any property possessed by a female Hindu, whether acquired before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be held by her as full owner thereof and not as a limited owner.
Section 15 General rules of succession in the case of female Hindus The property of a female Hindu dying intestate shall devolve firstly upon the children (including the children of any deceased child) and the husband.
